_comment: Prototype: 'did account X post <phrase> in a window' on Bluesky (AT Protocol public AppView, no key, no login). Same shape as judge-proto/jason/term_sheet.json.
claim: The Bluesky account did:plc:z72i7hdynmk6r22z27h6tvur (bsky.app) publishes a top-level post whose text contains the phrase 'mainnet launch' with a server-indexed time between 2026-11-02T00:00:00Z and 2026-11-06T00:00:00Z.

elements.q: Do the exhibits show a top-level (non-reply) post by the pinned account whose text contains the phrase 'mainnet launch' (case-insensitive) and whose indexedAt time is on or after 2026-11-02T00:00:00Z and on or before 2026-11-06T00:00:00Z?

custom_definitions: Deadline and window bounds are UTC instants pinned in the time block; 'UTC_V1' applies and no local time zone is ever read.
Early resolution: YES may be declared at the first qualifying post; NO may be declared only at/after the deadline and only with the coverage proof below.
Burden of proof is on YES: a post that is not shown in an admitted exhibit, or an ambiguous one, resolves NO, never YES by default.

Fallback: if the live fetch is unavailable or blocked, a keeper snapshot taken inside the window may be used; if neither is available the resolver reports COULDNT_CHECK and retries on the recovery ladder before VOID; a blocked or rate-limited page is never evidence of absence.
The account is identified by its DID (did:plc:z72i7hdynmk6r22z27h6tvur), never by handle; a handle change does not change which account is checked.
The time of a post is the AppView's indexedAt value. The author-set record createdAt is client-controlled and is never used to place a post inside or outside the window.
Only top-level posts count (feed filter posts_no_replies); replies, reposts and quote-posts of other accounts do not.
A post later deleted still counts as published if a keeper snapshot or archive exhibit captured it inside the window (RETRACTION_V1).

Coverage rule for NO: absence is proven only by a feed page fetched without a continuation cursor, or whose oldest item is indexed before the window start; a page that stops inside the window proves nothing.
